en.title: Amazon OA #340: Assign Requests to Servers
en.description: There are servers servers, numbered 0..servers−1. Process n requests in order: request i can only be assigned to a server numbered from 0 to requests[i] (inclusive), and it goes to the least busy one among them; if several are equally least busy, choose the one with the smallest number. A server's busyness is the number of requests already assigned to it, and assigned requests are never released. Output the server number each request is assigned to.
en.input: The first line contains two integers servers and n; the second line contains n integers requests[0..n−1]. 1≤servers≤100000, 1≤n≤200000, 0≤requests[i]<servers.
en.output: Output one line of n integers separated by spaces; the i-th is the server number assigned to request i.
en.explanation:
Example 1: servers=5, requests=[3,1,0,2,1]. For request 0, every server in 0..3 is idle, so choose 0; for request 1, server 1 is less busy within 0..1, so choose 1; request 2 can only choose 0; for request 3, server 2 has 0 assignments within 0..2, so choose 2; for request 4, within 0..1 server 0 has 2 and server 1 has 1, so choose 1. Output 0 1 0 2 1.
Example 2: all three servers are available, and the requests go to 0, 1 and 2 in turn; at the fourth request each of the three has 1, so choose 0.
Example 3: the first two requests can only use server 0; after that server 1 has the fewest assignments, so choose 1, then 2.
hints: A server's busyness is simply the number of requests assigned to it.
You need to query the minimum of (assignment count, number) over a prefix range.
A segment tree supports both prefix minimum queries and point updates.
